items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: Bud Freeman once told us that he heard Bessie singing

ctx.x: Do you recall some of the first tunes that you sang with these bands?

Well of course I sang “Ice Cream,” I sang “Baby Doll,” which is very sophisticated, Bessie Smith’s “Baby Doll,” “Young Woman Blues,” “Careless Love Blues,” “Alexander’s Ragtime Band” with the verse because that was so marvelous. I think there was a mistake on the original recording and they never cleared it up and I always thought that was fascinating. And then I sang a lot of things that really didn’t seem related to jazz but I felt that there was a possibility of making them in the idiom, which I still do with…

[sings] See you in my dreams, you know, it would have worked. And apparently according to Chris Albertson, who wrote the definitive book on Bessie, that she sang “Smoke Gets In Your Eyes,” and I don’t doubt it because people were required to sing all kinds of material.
